utility.title: Can we trust the latest reliability data?
sections: The question & reader
For an analyst reviewing utility reliability: which peer comparisons and data releases deserve to inform a decision?
Data
Six official EIA reliability workbooks, 2020–2025. The pipeline retains 11,552 method-specific records, source rows and missing values.
Approach
Python extraction, SQLite aggregation, method-consistent peer cohorts, state-total reconciliation and report-year-separated model testing. Utility-cluster resampling checks uncertainty.
What changed the decision

2023 and 2024 reconcile across all 51 available state summaries. Twenty-six 2025 summaries fall outside the 0.11-minute tolerance, so the 2025 release is excluded from decision inputs. The workbench uses 2024.
An important limit

The predictive candidate also fails its promotion gate: uncertainty crosses zero and nominal interval coverage falls short. The 2025 diagnostic uses a quarantined source year. No actual upgrade savings or engineering recommendation is established.
Delivery
A locally runnable API and a self-contained offline analyst workbench. The linked repository contains the implementation and verification evidence; it is not a public live application.

mortgage.title: Are we comparing lenders—or different borrowers?
sections: The question & reader
For consumer-finance research: which historical lender-price comparisons involve sufficiently similar observable borrower groups?
Data
123,445 public Houston-area HMDA originated-loan records from the pinned 2025 vintage. Product and completeness checks retain 32,095 eligible loans.
Approach

Python and SQL define a common product, select the five largest eligible lenders by counts and match loan amount, loan-to-value, debt-to-income and geography bands. Four hundred tract-level perturbations examine descriptive stability.
Finding

The five selected lenders have 9,344 eligible loans, but only 3,867 loans in 18 common-support cells. That is 41.38% retained. The observed price-spread range changes from 2.001 to 1.902 percentage points after matching.
Implication & limitations

Public matching leaves substantial selection and missing borrower information. These are descriptive historical differences, not lender effects or offers available today. Actual dated Loan Estimates are needed before recommending a lender.
Delivery
An offline rate, fee and holding-period workbench with a separate research report. Its scenarios are hypothetical, and the source repository is not a live lending application.

mobility.title: A better forecast. What changes in the plan?
sections: The question & reader
For an operations planner: does a better rental forecast improve a capacity rule when shortage and excess capacity carry different costs?
Data
731 daily observations from the UCI Bike Sharing dataset, covering historical 2011–2012 Capital Bikeshare rentals. Capacity costs are explicitly invented assumptions.
Approach

Five specifications are compared with chronological validation, rolling one-day-ahead forecasts and a separate 184-day test period. Validation selects ridge regression with penalty 1 before test results are reviewed.
Finding
The selected ridge model has test WAPE of 13.35%, compared with 18.70% for a seven-day seasonal baseline. Its nominal 90% prediction band covers 87.5% of test observations.
Implication & limitations

Forecast errors can be translated into conditional planning costs, but those modeled costs are not observed savings. The target is realized rentals, not unconstrained demand. Trip-equivalent capacity is not a physical bike-fleet recommendation.
Delivery
A reproducible Python pipeline, SQL analysis, CSV outputs and a downloadable HTML report. This is a historical benchmark, not a current forecasting service.

credit.title: When the simpler model wins.
sections: The question & reader
For credit-research model governance: do credit spreads improve recession classification beyond the Treasury curve and a simple historical recession probability?
Data
Pinned monthly FRED series for corporate spreads, Treasury yields and NBER recession labels. The research panel has 648 origins; testing uses 192 origins from 2008–2023, with labels through 2024.
Approach

Expanding logistic estimation uses prior-month features, a twelve-month label gap, training-only standardization and separate penalty selection. Paired blocks examine sensitivity to overlapping recession targets.
Finding
The credit-plus-curve candidate has Brier loss 0.1676. It improves on the curve model at 0.1750 but loses to the expanding historical baseline at 0.1487. Lower loss is better.
Decision & limitations

Withhold model promotion. The paired uncertainty band crosses zero, and the test has only two positive target runs. Revised data and eventual NBER labels do not reproduce a real-time information set. This is not a current recession forecast or validated trading signal.
Delivery
An offline review-threshold workbench, source-audited analysis and a reproducible Python/SQL workflow. Full methods and limitations are available in the repository.
